title: QUIC RFC 9000 Server 0-RTT Transport Parameter Acceptance Policy
purpose: Describe the bounded server-side policy that rejects 0-RTT acceptance when current server transport parameters cannot support the client's remembered values.
design_summary: QuicZeroRttTransportParameterPolicy now evaluates whether a server can accept 0-RTT against a remembered client transport-parameter snapshot. The decision rejects missing remembered or current server parameters, rejects reductions to required 0-RTT limits from Section 18.2, rejects reductions to restored optional max_idle_timeout and max_udp_payload_size values, rejects removal of a remembered disable_active_migration value, and exposes a separate helper for checking whether the advertised values actually provide non-zero client application-data allowance for 0-RTT.
data_and_state_considerations: The policy is stateless and uses effective RFC defaults where the current runtime already models defaults: absent active_connection_id_limit is treated as 2 and absent max_udp_payload_size is treated as the version 1 default. Absent flow-control and stream-limit parameters are treated as zero because those values block application-data sending until later MAX_DATA, MAX_STREAM_DATA, or MAX_STREAMS frames.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The helper rejects reduced required limits before optional restored-value reductions so failures remain deterministic.
The current bool model for disable_active_migration can only prove the remembered-present case; explicit false and absence are not distinguishable in QuicTransportParameters.
The application-data allowance check requires connection-level send credit plus either bidirectional client-send stream allowance or unidirectional client-send stream allowance.
No public early-data API, TLS early_data extension admission, server anti-replay store, or 0-RTT application delivery is introduced by this slice.
risks: This slice provides the server acceptance policy seam but does not yet wire a public server early-data admission feature.
Future transport parameters that affect 0-RTT application data need explicit comparison rules before the server can safely accept early data.
The remaining updated-value-in-0-RTT violation requirements still need a separate sender/receiver packet-context policy slice.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S7P4P1-0005 through REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-0351 as an internal server policy and proof slice. It deliberately leaves REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-0345 and REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S7P4P1-0010 through REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-0356 to follow-on client updated-value and packet-context enforcement work.
